sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Automotive Replacement Parts and Tuning Accessories

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (national level; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Civil Law foundation and corporate statutes with strong Common Law influence in commercial, maritime, and contractual practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (implemented via Law 254 of 2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended; Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (creation of the Financial Analysis Unit - UAF); Decree Law 2 of 10 December 2015, as amended (AML/CFT regime); Law 254 of 27 October 2021 and Executive Decree 29 of 16 February 2023 (UBO Registry for foundations, administered by the Ministry of Commerce and Industries - MICI).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the Founder's passport and national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the Founder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for countries party to the 1961 Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the competent Panamanian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution in the Founder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization per the issuing country's regime

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter attesting the Founder's relationship, conduct, and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization, or authenticated by the issuing bank's compliance department on bank letterhead where accepted by the resident agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency, certificate of good standing, and board resolution (required only if a corporate Founder is used)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registrar of the corporate Founder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Spanish translation of all non-Spanish documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian licensed sworn translator (traductor jurado) or consular-accredited translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille / Consular Legalization chain certified by the translating authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the Founder, Foundation Council members, Protector, and identified Beneficiaries against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU and UK consolidated lists, and Panama's national sanctions database maintained by the UAF. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP), close relatives, and close associates, including senior-management approval by the resident agent and documented source of funds and source of wealth. Basis: Law 23 of 2015, Decree Law 2 of 2015 (as amended), and UAF guidance for obliged entities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Sede Electrónica / online name deposit service (regpub.gob.pa), filed exclusively through a licensed resident agent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names may be adopted in any language using Latin script; the name must be singular and distinct, not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered entity. Foreign-language charter documents are filed in Spanish translation and must be sworn-translated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the resident agent must file, within five (5) business days of notification, a written reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) before the Director General of the Registro Público, attaching evidence of non-conflict and any required ministerial or supervisory authorization. Alternatively, a new name deposit for a different name may be submitted (a fresh fee applies). An extension of the initial 30-day reservation may be requested prior to expiry; a second renewal is at the sole discretion of the Registro.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The statutory registered office cannot be a virtual office; it must be a physical address in Panama, typically the licensed resident agent's premises. Virtual administrative or back-office arrangements and remote management from abroad are permissible for the e-commerce operations, but are not acceptable as the statutory registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: the foundation itself has no physical operating site, so unannounced inspection of the foundation is estimated at 5-10% in any 12-month cycle; the resident agent's office is subject to unannounced UAF AML/CFT inspections at an estimated 20-30% annual likelihood.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name deposit and availability certificate at the Registro Público de Panamá
Notarization of the foundation charter (Acta de Fundación) before a Panamanian notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public of the Republic of Panama

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Inscription of the foundation charter in the Registro Público, including electronic filing and microfilming fees
Licensed resident agent services and registered office (year one)
KYC/AML CDD compilation, UBO identification, PEP screening, and risk assessment by the resident agent
Notarization, apostille, or consular legalization of Founder's passport, address proof, bank reference, and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Overseas competent authorities / Panamanian consulates / notaries
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 30-60 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of non-Spanish documents into Spanish
UBO registry filing on the MICI final beneficiary platform

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (Ley 25 de 1995 sobre Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended; applicable articles: 1 (legal nature), 4 (legal personality), 6 (creation inter vivos), 7 (charter content), 8 (registered office and resident agent), 9 (registration), 12 (foundation council), and 13 (protector)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) — Foundations Section (Sección de Fundaciones), dependent on the Ministry of Government and Justice
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public, with appended Foundation Regulations (Reglamento de la Fundación); inscription through the Public Registry of Panama
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Charter capital must be at least USD 10,000 (or equivalent in balboas). Legal practice requires 25% of the capital to be paid up or definitively contributed at execution; no escrow account is mandated — capital may be satisfied by declaration of monetary or non-monetary assets of the founder, evidenced in the notarial act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The Founder hereby establishes a Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 12 June 1995. The initial capital of USD 10,000 is subscribed and fully paid by contribution of intangible assets. The Foundation Regulations are adopted in plenary and annexed to this Charter. The Registered Office is fixed at the offices of [Resident Agent], Panama City, Republic of Panama. The Foundation Council is appointed, comprising the Founder and two alternates, with full administrative and disposal powers. A Protector is appointed to safeguard beneficiary interests. The Council is authorized to open bank accounts, designate signatories, and instruct counsel to file the Foundation Charter with the Public Registry of Panama.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Notarization, and Execution of the Private Interest Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (appointed by the Supreme Court of Justice), acting jointly with licensed Panamanian corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a licensed Panamanian attorney to draft the Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) and Foundation Regulations (Reglamento) in Spanish. Submit the founder's identification and the program of the foundation's e-commerce object to the drafting attorney; approve the beneficiary schedule, Protector appointment, and Foundation Council composition; execute the instrument before the notary, who verifies the founder's identity, the subscribed capital declaration of USD 10,000, and the compliance of the charter-in-escrow; obtain two notarized certified copies for registry presentation and one for the resident agent.
required_dossiers: Valid passport of the founder
Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) in Spanish, in duplicate
Foundation Regulations (Reglamento) annex, in duplicate
Statement of initial capital subscription (USD 10,000)
Remote-execution power of attorney for the resident agent, if the founder is absent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a formal objection (e.g., defective capital clause, missing registered office, or vague corporate purpose), rectify the instrument by marginal amendment and re-execute before the same notary within two business days; the corrected notarial act supersedes the previous version for all registry purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Government Stamp Duties and Statutory Registration Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directorate General of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos — DGI) and the National Bank of Panama (Banco Nacional de Panamá) authorized collection counters for fiscal stamps
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calculate registration stamp duties on the notarized Foundation Charter; acquire the corresponding fiscal stamped paper through the DGI/Banco Nacional windows; place and cancel the fiscal stamps on the original charter, noting the paid duty; retain the official receipt (recibo oficial) and the stamp-cancellation page; attach the fee evidence to the charter before presentation to the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter bearing stamped and canceled fiscal paper
Official payment receipt (recibo oficial) issued by Banco Nacional de Panamá
Stamp-duty computation worksheet prepared by corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the DGI identifies underpaid duty or improperly canceled stamps, pay the differential plus the statutory surcharge at the DGI collection window and obtain a solvency certificate (constancia de pago); the amended stamped instrument is then re-presented to the registry without re-notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Foundation Charter at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) — Foundations Section (Sección de Fundaciones)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the stamped notarized Foundation Charter together with duplicate Foundation Regulations to the Foundations Section; pay the Public Registry fee per the official tariff; obtain the application's entry folio (ficha de inscripción); await the substantive review by the Registrar; upon approval, the registry issues the Certificate of Registration (Certificado de Registro) declaring that the private interest foundation is legally and validly constituted with its own legal personality.
required_dossiers: Original notarized and stamped Foundation Charter plus two certified copies
Foundation Regulations annex (original plus two certified copies)
Proof of payment of the Public Registry fee
Identity documentation and license copy of the resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the instrument with observations (nota de reparo) — e.g., missing beneficiary clause, capital irregularity, or incomplete resident-agent qualification — counsel files a corrective margin note (nota marginal) for approval within 10 working days; alternatively, the founder may re-present the corrected charter within 30 days, with a fresh fee payment for re-examination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Resident Agent and Establishment of the Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Resident Agent qualification supervised by the Registry and the Supreme Court of Justice roll of attorneys)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panamanian lawyer or licensed corporate-services firm to serve as Resident Agent (Agente Residente); fix the Registered Office at the resident agent's Panama City office address as required by Article 8 of Law 25; execute an acceptance letter and file it with the Registry together with the power of attorney; the registered office and agent details become part of the registry folio and appear on the Certificate of Registration.
required_dossiers: Resident agent acceptance letter (carta de aceptación)
Power of attorney designating the resident agent
Copy of the resident agent's professional license (idóneo) or firm registration
Registered-office address declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects the resident agent's qualification (e.g., expired professional license), the founder appoints an alternative duly licensed attorney and files a substitute acceptance within five working days; the original folio receives a marginal annotation without restarting the registration process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Fiscal and Operational Formalization (RUC, Municipal Notice, and Bank Account Opening)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directorate General of Revenue (DGI) under the Ministry of Economy and Finance; Municipality of Panama (Aviso de Operación, if local warehouse operation); Superintendence of Banks of Panama (banking authorization framework)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Registration, apply online at the DGI Sede Electrónica portal for the foundation's tax identification number (RUC); complete the registration form with the foundation object ISIC 4791 and the resident agent address; if the foundation operates a physical warehouse or distribution hub in Panama, file the municipal Aviso de Operación with the Municipality of Panama and obtain the municipal license; when RUC is issued, open a Panamanian corporate bank account under the authority of the Foundation Council resolution, listing authorized signatories; register the Stripe/PayPal payment processors against the foundation's articles and KYC documentation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration (Certificado de Registro) issued by the Public Registry
Certified copy of the notarized Foundation Charter
Foundation Council minutes appointing signatories and bankers
Resident agent's certification of the registered office
Passports of the Foundation Council members and the founder
RUC application form (Solicitud de Inscripción de Contribuyente)
Aviso de Operación form and municipal fee payment, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI challenges the foundation's economic substance because of nil local activities, file an explanatory letter annexing the charter and an economic-substance declaration confirming that all revenue stems from foreign digital platform sales; if the municipality conditions the Aviso de Operación on fire or zoning inspection of a selected warehouse, comply with the inspection or migrate to a third-party logistics (3PL) arrangement, which eliminates the municipal licensing trigger.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) — Directorate General of Industry (Dirección General de Industrias); ISIC 4791 online automotive-parts retail is classified as a commercial rather than an industrial activity, so no industrial operating license is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for ISIC 4791 e-commerce distribution; an optional municipal 'Aviso de Operación' (Notice of Operation) and annual municipal business license are required only if the foundation operates a local warehouse, delivery hub, or physical pick-up point within a Panamanian municipality.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente — MiAMBIENTE), Directorate of Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 0 — Exempt (no EIA, no Environmental Impact Report, and no Environmental Registration required); online retail and 3PL warehousing of automotive replacement parts without manufacturing, painting, or battery handling are not listed in Annex I of Executive Decree 123-2021.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Where a distribution warehouse is used: no process wastewater discharge threshold applies under Executive Decree 123-2021; VOC emissions must remain at de minimis (no surface-coating operation); packaging waste and returned parts must be managed per Law 1 of 2018 (integrated waste management) and segregated for recycling at the 3PL site; storage of oil-contaminated parts must comply with MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0343 wastewater protection limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Per SINAPROC (National Civil Protection System) Decree No. 761 of 2011, a fire-safety certification is required only for physical warehouses exceeding 1,000 m² or storing substantial combustible materials; for leased 3PL premises the operator holds the fire-certification duty. MITRADEL (Ministry of Labor and Labor Development) issues occupational hygiene and safety clearance for any local staff; hand-packing and administrative operations are subject to basic OSH standards (Executive Decree No. 314/2019). Pure drop-shipping operations with no local premises are exempt from physical inspections but remain subject to MITRADEL general worker protections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos (ANIP) — successor to the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) since October 2023; official portal: https://anip.gob.pa; electronic filing platform: E-TAX 4.0 (e-tax.anip.gob.pa); customs matters are administered by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is not automatically registered for tax purposes. It must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) only if it engages in taxable economic activities generating Panamanian-source income or performs taxable supplies in Panama. The foundation's Resident Agent prepares a certified copy of the foundation deed (public deed registered with the Registro Público de Panamá), the nomination documents of the foundation council members, and the ITBMS/income-tax registration application, and files them through the ANIP E-TAX portal or at ANIP service windows. ANIP issues a single RUC consolidating income-tax, ITBMS, and customs-obligation status. A purely passive or foreign-source PIF (selling auto parts abroad) may lawfully remain unregistered; it should obtain a written 'non-taxpayer status' confirmation from ANIP where required by foreign counterparties or payment processors (Stripe/PayPal).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama applies a mandatory territorial-source classification; no US-style check-the-box election exists. A PIF may elect to become a regular registered taxpayer by applying for a RUC and may opt into the simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS regime if eligible by turnover. No hybrid-mismatch elections are available; Panama does not adopt OECD hybrid rules, but CFC and transfer-pricing rules (Law 254 of 2021; Law 52 of 2016) apply to offshore-controlled entities. Advanced pricing agreements and administrative rulings are available from ANIP for cross-border transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panamanian value-added tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PTY 0 — no de minimis monetary threshold; any person, including a non-resident PIF, performing taxable supplies of movable goods or services within Panamanian territory must register for ITBMS as of the first taxable operation. A PIF whose auto-parts sales are entirely destined for foreign buyers and physically exported from Panama is not required to register solely for those export operations. Physical imports of goods into Panama are subject to ITBMS at the 7% rate at customs, irrespective of importer registration status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) through ANIP-certified billing software or the free ANIP E-TAX portal. Every invoice must be transmitted to ANIP in near-real time for validation and issuance of a digital signature, unique security code, and QR code. In-store point-of-sale receipts may be produced via ANIP-authorized fiscal printers (impresoras fiscales) with daily settlement upload. Export operations are separately reported through the Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior (VUCE) and the ANA customs clearance system; no additional tax-stamping applies to exported goods.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% ITBMS rate applies to: (i) tangible goods physically exported from Panama and released by ANA under an accepted export declaration, provided the PIF is registered as exporter and title and risk pass to a non-resident buyer; (ii) services rendered in Panama to non-resident recipients whose benefit is wholly realized and exploited abroad; (iii) supplies to Colon Free Zone operators, international transportation, and diplomatic missions. The zero-rating claim requires proof that the goods left Panamanian customs territory within the statutory period and that export proceeds were collected within 180 days.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduana, DUA) accepted and validated by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing physical departure from Panamanian customs territory
Commercial invoice, packing list, and purchase order or written contract with the foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement proving collection of export proceeds in USD (USD is legal tender in Panama) within the 180-day deadline
Exporter registration certificate with ANA and ANIP, plus a schedule of zero-rated export invoices supporting any ITBMS credit/refund claim
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ANIP and ANA may audit zero-rated export transactions for up to five years (extendable in cases of fraud). Failure to substantiate physical export or foreign-source benefit causes the transaction to be recharacterized as a domestic taxable sale, giving rise to ITBMS at 7%, monthly statutory interest, and fines of up to 100% of the omitted tax. Any ITBMS input-credit refund improperly claimed from zero-rated exports is retrospectively clawed back with a surcharge. Knowingly submitting fictitious export declarations, false DUA filings, or non-existent foreign buyers constitutes tax fraud and customs fraud, punishable under Panamanian criminal and customs statutes, with imprisonment of 2–5 years, criminal fines, and forfeiture of the goods or their value, in addition to loss of the right to export zero-rating for a compliance term.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No standalone central bank exists in Panama. The Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá) is the primary banking and foreign exchange regulatory authority. The National Bank of Panama (Banco Nacional de Panamá) acts as fiscal agent for the Republic.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy; the US dollar is legal tender alongside the Balboa (pegged 1:1). Both current account and capital account transactions are freely convertible. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and capital repatriation are unrestricted, subject to documentary compliance with anti-money laundering rules, OFAC screening, and Panama's territorial income tax regime. No prior Central Bank approval is required for cross-border transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama operates a dollarized monetary system without exchange controls. Exporters are not subject to any statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; receipts may be retained in USD or any other currency at the exporter's discretion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium feasibility. Panama Law No. 42 of 2021 introduced an authorization regime for innovation service providers, including digital payment facilitators; an offshore digital EMI without a Panama license cannot lawfully conduct banking or payment services. A Private Interest Foundation may, however, utilize licensed local banks as primary settlement rails and integrate global payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal) via commercial merchant accounts. Account opening with unregulated foreign EMIs is generally discouraged and may trigger stringent KYC scrutiny.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is not an absolute mandatory for all onboarding; however, most tier-1 Panamanian banks require at least one in-person interview for directors/officers of the foundation or a locally qualified representative. Remote opening is permissible for low-risk, non-PEP clients when supported by apostilled corporate documents and notarized proof of identity, but biometric video identification and independent verification through a correspondent bank are typically required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation perceived as a shell entity lacking economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized foundation deed, foundation regulations, minutes of the foundation council, audited or CPA-reviewed financial statements, active General Directorate of Revenue (DGI) registration, e-commerce marketplace transaction reports, supplier/distributor contracts, and logistics invoices demonstrating real business activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Obscure beneficial ownership structure, including nominee officers or bearer-like arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Register of Beneficial Owners under Law 169 of 2019 (amended by Law 129 of 2020), sworn declarations identifying founders, protectors, and beneficiaries, apostilled passports, proof of residential address, and letters of consent from all relevant parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk trade counterparties, particularly cross-border suppliers in jurisdictions with enhanced monitoring (e.g., PRC).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade continuity file containing supplier business licenses, bank reference letters, commercial invoices, bills of lading, inspection certificates, and a documented country risk assessment with executed mitigation measures, including SWIFT correspondent bank confirmations of all payment counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed as USD wires via SWIFT MT103 from the founder/treasury account. Pacment purpose codes should follow the Project/AAST treasury classifications; acceptable narratives include 'Capital Contribution to Foundation', 'Subordinate Loan to Foundation', or 'Advance Against Participation'. The receiving bank must obtain supporting board resolution, foundation deed extracts, and source-of-funds declarations. Basel III depository verification includes OFAC sanctions screening and CFATF-compliant beneficial ownership confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments under USD 500,000 are settled through SWIFT MT103 clean payments. Larger consignments use irrevocable commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) issued by a Panamanian bank and confirmed by the beneficiary's correspondent bank (e.g., China, Taiwan, USA). Each L/C drawing is secured by compliant commercial invoices, transport documents, and certificate of origin. Payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal) settle in USD via direct ACH or SWIFT aggregations to the operational account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on CNY and KRW
FX Options (Over-the-Counter), including puts and calls on major convertible currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Government Tax (Panama Private Interest Foundation annual state fee under Law 25 of 1995)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama General Directorate of Revenue (DGI), remitted through the licensed Registered Agent and credited to the Public Registry good-standing record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable no later than 15 July of each calendar year for the preceding year; no income-based calculation is required, and the fee is a flat government charge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% flat surcharge; repeated non-payment for consecutive periods may result in the Public Registry recording an adverse state and eventually striking the foundation from the Private Interest Foundation Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation Return (Declaración de Información del Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama General Directorate of Revenue (DGI) - Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the DGI filing window set in the first quarter; generally the confirmation must be completed by 15-31 March, and a nil-change return is still required if no beneficial ownership movements occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing is subject to administrative fines of up to USD 5,000, and the foundation's good-standing certificates and banking instructions may be blocked until the confirmation is submitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Register and Accounting Memorial Verification (corporate secretarial certificate issued by the Registered Agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Panamanian Registered Agent; records remain available for inspection by the Public Registry and DGI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the foundation's incorporation anniversary, or within 15 working days upon formal inspection request of the Public Registry or DGI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to produce the foundation charter, books, or accounting memorial on request can lead to an adverse public-registry certificate, tax inspection penalties, and, in serious cases, criminal sanctions for concealment of accounting records

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Panama Private Interest Foundation is not automatically obliged to appoint an external auditor. An independent certified audit becomes mandatory only if the foundation charter requires it, a Panamanian bank or creditor requires it, or the foundation earns Panamanian-source gross income above the statutory audit threshold applicable to commercial legal entities (generally USD 3,000,000), in which case DGI may demand audited financial statements. The e-commerce auto-parts activity, if executed wholly outside Panama in a territorial non-resident structure, does not by itself create a statutory audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as endorsed by the Technical Accounting Committee of Panama (CATEC); smaller non-public-interest entities may apply IFRS for SMEs. The PIF must maintain internal accounting records and an accounting memorial consistent with generally accepted accounting practice in Panama.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Panama PIF has no share capital and no shareholders. Economic ownership is expressed through the foundation charter, foundation-council composition, protectors, and named beneficiaries. Any change of beneficiary, protector, or assignment of foundation economic rights must be documented in a notarized resolution or charter amendment, registered at the Public Registry, and updated in the DGI Beneficial Owner Registry within the statutory update period. Independently of changes, the foundation must submit an annual confirmation reflecting all natural-person ultimate beneficiaries, with the registered agent performing the lawful-control and risk-tier review before each filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation Charter (public instrument) and Foundation Regulations
Register of Founders and Foundation Council Members
Register of Beneficiaries and Protector(s)/Supervisory Council

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutory for a non-operating PIF; an optional certified audit normally ranges from USD 2,500 to USD 7,500 depending on asset size and transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies progressive corporate income tax (CIT) rates under Law 13 of 2019: 15% on the first B/.50,000 of taxable income; 17% on B/.50,001-100,000; 19% on B/.100,001-200,000; 21% on B/.200,001-500,000; 23% on B/.500,001-1,000,000; and 25% on taxable income exceeding B/.1,000,000. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) under Law 25 of 1995 is taxable only on Panamanian-source income under the territorial system (Tax Code Art. 694); foreign-source e-commerce income, including retail sales consummated and delivered abroad, is outside the CIT net. The annual PIF flat fee of B/.400 satisfies the annual tax obligation for non-operating foundations. Optional simplified small-taxpayer regime (REPS) may apply where annual gross receipts do not exceed B/.200,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 157 (Declaración de Renta, Ganancias y Pérdidas) - annual corporate income tax return filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax portal (etaxdgi.dgi.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and payment are due within three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique taxpayer registration number (Registro Único del Contribuyente) of the PIF.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF must hold an active RUC before filing; a non-resident-owned PIF uses its Panama RUC and the domicile of its resident agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from sales, services, or any economic activity performed or consummated within Panamanian territory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include online retail proceeds only where goods are delivered into Panama or the sale is negotiated and consummated in Panama; Stripe/PayPal receipts from foreign customers with foreign delivery addresses are foreign-source and excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income derived from sources outside Panama; exempt under the territorial system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign e-commerce turnover here as informational where the PIF holds Panamanian-source income; retain country-level records, logistics proofs, and payment statements of Stripe/PayPal to support the extraterritorial character.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs, expenses, and charges economically linked to Panamanian-source income, supported by invoices and accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate the cost of goods, freight, payment-gateway fees, and fulfillment costs against Panamanian-source revenue; foreign-source cost allocation must be clearly documented to avoid the DGI's proportional re-attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panamanian-source gross income minus allowable deductions and applicable loss carryforwards (maximum five years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Law 13 of 2019 progressive brackets; losses from foreign-source activities cannot be used against Panamanian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT computed at the applicable 15%-25% progressive rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No tax arises where Box 2 is nil; a nil Form 157 is mandatory even when the PIF is fully foreign-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Monthly advance payments (Formulario 156) and any prior withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recoverable credits require proof of remittance through the DGI system; foreign-source-only PIFs may demonstrate zero prepayment obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of CIT due after advance payments, or refundable credit balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is executed in Panamanian balboas at the collection desk of the DGI portal; non-resident PIFs must maintain a local payment channel or instruct the resident agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is sanctioned with fines of B/.50 to B/.5,000 under Tax Code Art. 706, plus monthly mora surcharges and compensatory interest of 1% per month on unpaid tax; failure to pay the determined tax triggers enforced collection, definitive assessment ex officio, and temporary suspension of the RUC and import/export authorizations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 156 (Pago Anticipado Mensual de la Renta) - monthly advance income tax payment filed through the DGI e-Tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due the 15th business day of the month following the taxable month; taxpayers under the simplified regime may make advance payments quarterly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same RUC as the annual return; no monthly payment is due when the PIF has no Panamanian-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line B - Gross Panamanian-source receipts of the period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross cash and electronic payment receipts subject to the advance payment base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-source card settlement amounts; maintain Stripe/PayPal merchant summaries showing card-holder country, shipping destination, and gateway fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Higher of the 2% statutory coefficient on gross Panamanian receipts or the coefficient determined from the preceding annual return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the PIF's e-commerce activity is entirely foreign-source, the computed amount is zero and no monthly form is required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file and pay the monthly advance results in a fine of B/.50 to B/.5,000, monthly mora interest at 1%, and potential denial of the annual return's advance-payment credit; continued default can trigger DGI provisional assessment based on bank and payment-gateway records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 185 (Anexo de Precios de Transferencia) - annual transfer-pricing information and documentation declaration filed electronically with the DGI.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed concurrently with Formulario 157, within three months after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate value of transactions carried out during the year with related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where aggregate related-party dealings exceed B/.1,000,000, the annex is mandatory; a foreign-only e-commerce operation dealing with an overseas supplier under common control must analyze the supply contract, warehouse fees, and payment-gateway charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arm's-length method applied per transaction category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CUP is preferred for online retail of automotive parts and tuning accessories; TNMM is accepted where comparables exist; the analysis must be documented even if no Form 185 is due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reference to contracts, invoices, and comparability adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF must retain supplier agreements, pricing lists, freight documents, and gateway fee schedules to sustain the transaction reality of each related-party flow.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 185 or to produce the Local File on demand triggers penalties of B/.10,000 to B/.100,000 plus the recharacterization of the transaction at market value with the 25% CIT and mora surcharges; deliberate omission is treated as tax evasion under Art. 706-A.
